about: The outcome classes of one generation, as a machine sees them (docs/adr/0087, section 9.4).
A model's answer reaches a machine only through the answer schema and the host operation,
so at each call the machine sees one of a finite set of classes: a record read, a refusal of
each code a schema of fields reaches, an answer cut by `length`, each failure code, the
refusal, a deadline that passes, and a cancel by leaving the state. The exhaustive provider
of every lane's reference host stands for a model that may give any class at any call: the
test names a sequence of classes, each start takes the next one, and the provider answers
what the class says. Every lane runs `machine` against every sequence of classes up to
`bound` and holds what the machine publishes after each call to the class's `expect`.
Each class is one `end`: `answer` (a completion with `text` and `finish`, the provider
unconstrained, its tokens the bytes of the prompt and of the text, `model` `exhaustive`),
`failure` (a completion whose `error` is the code), `refusal` (the host declines to start
it, `invalid_argument`) or `hold` (the provider does not answer; `then` says how the call
ends: `advance`, the engine's clock moved `deadline_ms` on, or `leave`, the event `leave`).
Each call is the event `ask.event` with `ask.data`, a request the host accepts.
`expect` is what the machine publishes after the call: `outcome`, `why` and `finish`, and
`answer` where the call reads a record. A call that reads none leaves `answer` as the last
call that read one left it, `null` before any; `calls` is the call's number from 1, and the
machine is in `idle`. The texts and their refusals are those of
sce-build/tests/fixtures/static_datamodel/scenarios/static_lift.json, against the same
schema. `deferred` names a refusal code the machine's answer schema does not reach, and why.
`notOffered` is a record the lift reads whose `id` (99) is not one the reference harness
offers, which holds the `read` class's id (7) alone (docs/adr/0087, section 6.1 item 2).
`machine` has no check of its own and reads it as `read`; it is a class of its own because
the harness's check tells it apart from a record it accepts. `harness` is what the exhaustive
run of the reference harness reads beside the classes (docs/adr/0087, Landing order item 7):
the harness `machine`, the event that `start`s it with its `data`, the event it is `offer`ed
an id by and the ids it is `offered` (each `{"id": n}`, before the start), the state whose
invoke is the `call` (a call site is a row of the harness's transition table whose `targets`
is that state, so each call is made through the row the run entered it by),
its attempt `bound` (`harness_attempts`), which no run's calls pass, how a held call is left
(`then`, as a class's, for either class that holds: `advance` moves the engine's clock
`deadline_ms` on, past the call's own deadline) and that deadline. There is one table: the
harness run reads its classes from here, every sequence of `bound` classes, each a run.
Expected values are derived from the specification, not observed from a host.

deferred.why: a list past its bound: the answer schema every lane's machine lifts holds a list once every lane holds a variable of a record that holds one (docs/adr/0087, Landing order item 8)

a list short of its lower count: the answer schema every lane's machine lifts holds a list once every lane holds a variable of a record that holds one (docs/adr/0086, section 15.11; docs/adr/0087, Landing order item 8)
